input.quote: No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
input.rationale: Sections 14.1-14.4 and 13.2 satisfy most of the preferred position: Customer owns and Vendor assigns Deliverables (14.2), Vendor keeps only its pre-existing Vendor Technology (14.3, definition 1.9), Customer owns Customer Data (14.1), no joint ownership absent a signed instrument (14.4), and 13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor Technology. The one material failure is the scope of Vendor's rights in Customer Data: 14.1 licenses processing to \"improve the Services\", and 15.1 permits processing \"as permitted by this Agreement\" and model training on Customer Data with consent, all of which extend beyond processing solely to provide the Services. Our redline narrows those three expansions and leaves the ownership and licence bargain intact.

proposal.summary: Limit Vendor's licence in Customer Data to processing solely to provide the Services
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that any Vendor right in Customer Data must be limited to processing it solely to provide the Services, so we removed the "improve the Services", "as permitted by this Agreement", and consent-based model-training expansions. Ownership, assignment and the perpetual embedded-IP licence are already acceptable and untouched.

Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.

mappings.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
mappings.quote: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

mappings.quote: perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence

mappings.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
mappings.quote: As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services.

mappings.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
